title: Correct radial force expression
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be $F_r = mg\cos\theta_0 - \frac{m v^2}{R}$ or an algebraically equivalent form.

title: Correct maximum angle expression
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be $\alpha_{\max} = \frac{r}{R \sin \theta_0} \sqrt{1 - \frac{mgR(1-\cos\theta_0) - \frac{1}{2}mgR\theta_0\sin\theta_0}{K}}$ or an algebraically equivalent form.

title: Radial force balance reasoning
description: Important: The solution must identify the radial components of gravity ($mg\cos\theta_0$) and the centripetal/centrifugal force ($-mv^2/R$) from motion along a latitude.

title: Energy conservation setup
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must apply energy conservation, equating initial energy (gravitational, spring potential, launch kinetic) to final energy at the cylinder (gravitational and kinetic).

title: Angular momentum conservation
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must apply angular momentum conservation about the vertical axis to relate the launch conditions to the tangential speed at the cylinder ($m v \sin\alpha (R\sin\theta_0) = m u r$).

title: Spring equilibrium substitution
description: Important: The solution must use the given equilibrium condition (spring force balances gravity component) to substitute $\frac{1}{2}kR^2\theta_0^2$ with $\frac{1}{2}mgR\theta_0\sin\theta_0$ in the energy equation.

title: Small-angle approximation for kinetic energy
description: Optional: The solution may note the use of the approximation $\sin\alpha \approx \alpha$ and $K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ when expressing the final rotational kinetic energy term.

title: Sign error in radial force
description: Pitfall: Deduct points if the sign of the centripetal term is incorrect (e.g., written as $+\frac{mv^2}{R}$) in the radial force expression.

title: Missing energy or momentum term
description: Pitfall: Deduct points if the energy conservation or angular momentum conservation equation omits a major term (e.g., spring potential, gravitational potential difference, or tangential velocity relation).

title: Incorrect trigonometric component
description: Pitfall: Deduct points for an incorrect trigonometric factor in the centripetal force (e.g., using $\sin\theta_0$ or $\cos\theta_0$ incorrectly) or in the angular momentum arm ($R\sin\theta_0$).
